title: Three Siblings Board IndiGo Flight, Find Rahul Dravid in Front Row
excerpt: Aayush, Aashna and Aagam Agarwal were flying home to Jaipur after a family wedding in Hyderabad when the former India captain, seated in the front row, spoke with them and posed for a photograph.
body:
• Three siblings — Aayush, Aashna and Aagam Agarwal — flew IndiGo from Hyderabad to Jaipur on Sunday, October 11, after a family wedding, and found Rahul Dravid seated in the front row.
  • Dravid spoke with the siblings and posed for a photograph with them, a moment that was shared widely on social media.
  • Despite a delayed arrival in Jaipur at about 3 a.m., the family described the flight as one they would cherish for a lifetime.

It was meant to be a routine flight home after a family wedding. Instead, three siblings boarding an IndiGo flight from Hyderabad to Jaipur on Sunday, October 11, found one of Indian cricket's most familiar faces in the front row: Rahul Dravid, the former India captain and head coach, travelling as a fellow passenger on the same aircraft.

A wedding trip with an unexpected co-passenger

Siblings Aayush, Aashna and Aagam Agarwal had been in Hyderabad for a family wedding, according to India Today's account of the flight. Their father had booked their tickets for the journey back to Jaipur. Nothing about the booking suggested the trip would be any different from any other domestic flight the family had taken together.

That changed once they boarded. Dravid, 53, was seated in the front row of the aircraft. For three siblings travelling together after a wedding, the sight of a cricketer many Indians grew up watching — first as a batsman, later as the coach who guided India to the T20 World Cup title in 2024 — turned a short hop home into the part of the wedding trip they are likely to retell most often.

A photograph, and a warm conversation

Dravid spoke with the siblings and posed for a photograph with them. The photograph was shared widely on social media, and coverage of the encounter, including a photo gallery, spread well beyond the passengers on that one flight. Separate reporting on Dravid meeting young fans on an IndiGo flight has also drawn millions of views online, a reminder of how reliably a quiet, courteous exchange with him travels, as CricketWinner's report on a similar viral flight moment noted.

For Aayush, though, the photograph was not the whole story. He said the photo "looked perfect," but added: "more than the photo, it was just his warm presence who enriched our experience by his endearing personality." It is a modest verdict, and it fits the encounter: no ceremony, no announcement on board, just a brief conversation and a picture with a passenger who happened to be in the front row.

A 3 a.m. arrival they say they will cherish

The journey itself was less smooth than the meeting. After a delay, the flight reached Jaipur at about 3 a.m., the kind of arrival time that normally becomes the complaint in a family travel story. Here, it became part of the keepsake. In a letter their father wrote to Dravid afterwards, that late arrival was framed very differently — as part of an experience the siblings would "cherish for a lifetime."

That framing explains why the story has travelled. Weddings produce hundreds of photographs; flights usually produce none worth keeping. This one produced both, capped by a delayed midnight landing nobody in the family seems to mind remembering.

nri_angle: For diaspora readers who grew up watching Rahul Dravid, a chance front-row meeting on a routine India domestic flight is the kind of small, warm travel moment families retell for years.
